question: The European Sky Shield Initiative (ESSI) is a welcome step towards collective defence, aiming to bring Member States together to set up an integrated air defence system. To date, more than 20 Member States have signed up. In Western Europe, France and Italy are among those who have yet to join.

This could jeopardise its effectiveness, turning it into a new ‘Maginot Line’, leaving an entire Western and Southern front exposed. With the threat of missile and drone attacks growing, time is of the essence in implementing these defence systems. In view of the above, can the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy/Vice-President of the Commission answer the following: 1.
What strategic value does the ESSI have?

From the perspective of wanting to strengthen the European defence technological and industrial base and make space for European defence technology champions, are there barriers to integrating the SAMP/T and PATRIOT systems, already used by NATO, within the ESSI?
Could a European air and missile rapid response force be created as a complementary deterrent to that of NATO?
answer: The European Sky Shield Initiative (ESSI) is not an EU initiative. It is coordinated by Germany and aims at setting up an integrated air defence system. Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine confirmed the criticality of this capability. The membership of ESSI as well as the exact systems to be used for building up ESSI’s architecture are decided upon by the participating countries.

At EU level, strengthening the multilayer Air and Missile Defence systems of Member States has been identified among the most urgent capability gaps in the Defence Investment Gaps Analysis of May 2022 (1). Integrated Air and Missile Defence is part of the 2023 EU Capability Development Priorities (2), agreed by the European Defence Agency Steering Board in November 2023.

Its critical importance was further stressed in the European Defence Industrial Strategy (EDIS) (3). Subject to Member States’ agreement, EDIS proposed to establish European Defence Projects of Common Interest to focus efforts and resources. This could include capabilities related to integrated European air and missile defence.

Furthermore, in line with the Strategic Compass (4), a strategic reflection to ensure a free, safe and secure European access to airspace was launched in 2023. The Council of the European Union, in its conclusions on security and defence adopted on 27 May 2024, looked forward to a proposal for a dedicated EU airspace strategy for security and defence with a view to its adoption in 2025 (5).

Within the EU framework, Member States remain in the lead for the capability planning and development. Cooperation with the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) and key partners remains the underlying principle.
